topic: Agyn Review 2026: Kubernetes-Native Runtime for AI Agents

key_points: Agyn is an open-source, Kubernetes-native agent orchestration platform (AGPL-3.0)
Runs any AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, custom) at scale with serverless execution
Terraform-managed declarative configuration (IaC)
Zero-trust networking where credentials never reach the LLM context
MCP servers in separate containers with per-tool credential isolation
Per-conversation sandboxing, RBAC, SSO, audit logs, spend caps
Built with TypeScript, 217 GitHub stars, launched May 2026
Academic paper: Agyn — An Open-Source Platform for AI Agents with Scalable On-Demand Execution, Agent Definition as a Code, and Zero-Trust Access
Authors: Nikita Benkovich, Vitalii Valkov
Three key principles: signal-driven stateful serverless runtime on K8s, Terraform provider for agent/harness definition, zero-trust/least-privilege security model
Agent-agnostic, model-agnostic, cloud-agnostic
Compares Agyn vs 6 competitors: AWS Bedrock AgentCore, Cloudflare Agents, Google AX, Anthropic Claude Managed Agents, kagent, Vercel Open Agents
Scored on 7 criteria: self-hosting, multi-vendor agents, per-MCP-server isolation, declarative config, serverless, credential isolation, zero-trust networking
No competitor scored above 3.75/7; only AgentCore cleared 3.0
Agyn is the only platform that refuses trade-offs between managed convenience and security
Defines AI agent runtime as the layer between program and OS that provides lifecycle, isolation, and governance
Distinguishes runtime from harness: runtime orchestrates, harness executes
Key runtime services: scheduling, sandboxing, networking, secrets management, observability
HN discussion: 9 points, 4 comments
Key question: 'core idea works only for Kubernetes?' — K8s dependency is a consideration
Community feedback: 'Agents are quickly becoming infra, not just local dev tools'
Question about adoption path from local Claude/Codex to K8s-native runtime

stats.fact: Agyn launched on GitHub in May 2026, reached 217 stars by July 2026
Built with TypeScript, uses OpenZiti + Istio for zero-trust networking
No competitor platform scored above 3.75/7 on production-readiness criteria
Agyn supports Claude Code, Codex, and custom agent containers out of the box
Agyn uses Terraform provider for agent and harness definition as code
Agyn provides per-MCP-server container isolation — each tool gets its own filesystem and process tree
Agyn's zero-trust model gives every agent its own x509 identity with deny-by-default access
Agyn has serverless scale-to-zero — agents spawn on message, terminate on idle
Agyn competes with Google AX, AWS Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Code Cloud, Cloudflare Agents, kagent, Vercel Open Agents

angles: Agyn fills the gap between local agent development and production deployment — the missing 'control plane' for enterprise AI agents
Unique differentiator: credential isolation where secrets never reach the LLM context (vs competitors that pass secrets through)
Kubernetes-native design means teams already on K8s can adopt without new infrastructure — but K8s dependency is a barrier for smaller teams
Open-source alternative to managed services (Google AX, AWS AgentCore) — appeals to regulated/sovereign deployments
The 'agent infrastructure as code' approach with Terraform provider enables GitOps workflows for agent fleets
MCP server isolation in separate containers is a security innovation not matched by any competitor
Agyn's architecture paper (arXiv) provides academic credibility and detailed design rationale
